newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles lower on cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles lower on cooler weather.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled lower Monday on outlook of temperatures easing in parts of the Northwest and key markets on the California seaboard, brokers and traders said.
"We're seeing prices a little lower. The heatwave in the Northwest is basically gone," said one Houston trader.
Expectations of cooler weather also pressured physical prices in the West lower, brokers and traders said.
September California-Oregon Border (COB) futures settled down 47 cents at $18.24 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trading between $18.20 and $18.60.
October COB ended at $16.40, down 31 cents. Other deferred COB closed five to 20 cents lower.
September Palo Verde (PV) finished at $21.08 per MWh, down 52 cents after hitting a session high of $21.60.
Back-month PV contracts settled 20 to 35 cents lower.
The ongoing capacity reduction on the 4,800 MW Pacific Intertie has had little effect on power prices in the Southwest today.
"Since there's little (incremental) demand in PV, it's not affecting them as a whole," the trader said.

The intertie, operated by Bonneville Power Administration and Pacific Gas and Electric Co, is the major line carrying hydroelectricity from the Northwest to northern and central California. The transmission path's capacity was cut Saturday, Aug 10, after a massive disturbance in the western power grid. The intertie was reportedly operating at 3,200 MW today.
Because of weaker fundamentals, September COB and PV futures will likely test supports at $18.00 and $21.00, respectively, before they expire Tuesday, brokers and traders said.
NYMEX estimated 164 COB and 178 PV were sold Monday.
